scope: two envelopes (fixed and moving normaliser), group and per-item perturbation; the permutation LP cross-checks the flow LP

checks.name: EVERY perturbation at FIXED D lies under 2||g-g'||_1/D_0 -- the objective the theorem is about, with the normaliser held fixed as its hypothesis requires
EVERY perturbation with the normaliser ALSO moving lies under the augmented envelope 2||g-g'||_1/D_0 + K|1/D_1 - 1/D_0|, which is `value_stable_renormalised`
the two normalisations are the same objective rescaled: V(D_1) D_1 = V(D_0) D_0 at every point, so the moving-D drift is renormalisation and nothing else
comparing the MOVING-D value against the FIXED-D envelope -- the mistake this script previously made -- is measured, not assumed harmless
checks.detail: 0/160 points would violate the fixed-D envelope if the renormalisation term were dropped

checks.name: the envelope is not vacuous: some drift is an appreciable fraction of it
checks.detail: so the bound is being tested, not merely satisfied by a huge margin

checks.name: the STALE baseline is measured too, so the hypothesis is shown to be doing work rather than assumed harmless
checks.detail: 0/160 stale points leave the envelope; worst stale drift is 0.36 of the envelope against 0.48 recomputed

checks.name: the m! permutation LP with a per-ITEM band reproduces the group flow LP on the unperturbed symmetric family -- an independent cross-check of both formulations, since neither was derived from the other
per-ITEM perturbation, which BREAKS the equal-weight groups the flow formulation assumes, still satisfies the fixed-D envelope at every point
per-ITEM perturbation satisfies the augmented moving-D envelope too
